Definition: middle voice from G1537 and G2910; to hang upon the lips of a speaker, i.e. listen closely:--be very attentive.
BiblicalUsage: This word means to hang upon the lips of a speaker, to listen so closely that you hang on every word, and it occurs once, for the crowds who heard Jesus in the temple. The chief priests and scribes seek to destroy Him and cannot find a way, because all the people are very attentive to hear Him, hanging on His words. One verb holds a whole crowd still.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe hanging on Jesus' words is the right posture, because the crowds who listened could not be moved by the priests who plotted.
